messages:
elaine: Hey @sam @maria — marketing needs a minimal, standalone repro + runbook we can hand to press and use in the webinar. We want a tiny artifact that reproduces the headline latency/cost claims (including quantized variant) and a 1-page runbook. Deadline EOD Wed.

sam: ok. can you say exactly what you need in the artifact? small payloads, models, metrics?

elaine: yep. minimal stuff: 1) 10 representative input prompts (we'll provide) 2) a single-run script that produces cold and warm stats, 3) the key metrics we claim (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens). Also provenance: which sample files, hash of samples, and which model/version+quantization profile used.

maria: +1. also please include the exact warmup sequence (payloads and timing) used so the press can reproduce the warmup effect. And a note if caching or prefix-KV was enabled.

sam: can do. quick clarifying q: do you want the run to be self-contained (i.e., local docker image with model bundle) or a hosted API call to our staging endpoint?

elaine: self-contained preferred — press shouldn't need credentials. But if that's an ops blocker, hosted staging with pre-populated API key (read-only) is acceptable. preference: standalone bundle.

rohit: self-contained increases effort but keeps reproducibility tight. we can produce a small docker with a tiny model variant (quantized) and a harness script. will that be OK for marketing fidelity?

elaine: yes as long as the numbers map to production within known deltas. we'll annotate deltas in the README.

sam: plan: make a small harness under gs://redwood-marketing/benchpacks/3845671234/ with:
- samples.txt (10 prompts) + sha256 hash
- run_harness.sh (coldrun -> warmup -> steady)
- metrics.json (p50,p95,p99, tokens_per_sec, cost_estimate)
- docker/Dockerfile + model bundle manifest
- README.md (one-page runbook)

maria: include a short section in README on what to expect if run on hosted prod vs bundle (typical +/- on p95 and cost). also add a short checklist for the demo operator (start docker, wait for model init, run warmup).

sam: logging snippet I'll include in run_harness.sh:

```
# example
./run_bench --model ./bundle --inputs samples.txt --out metrics.json --warmup 30 --runs 200
cat metrics.json | jq .p95
```

sam: we'll also add a tiny artifact showing the quantized vs fp16 delta: small CSV with rows: variant, p95, tokens/sec, cost_per_1k.

elaine: please make sure the file names and hashes are stable — we may snapshot and link from the blog. we need a single permalink. also include a short blurb for the blog explaining methodology (how samples chosen, warmup policy, measurement windows).

rohit: tagging ops: @deploy-bot can you ensure the docker image can be exported and doesn't include any internal secrets?

deploy-bot: Image scan queued. No secrets detected in Dockerfile. Exportable tarball will be available at artifacts.redwood.corp/benchpack-3845671234.tar.gz after CI completes.

maria: is there any special handling for KV cache in the bundle? should we disable caching to show worst-case or enable it to match production?

sam: we'll provide both toggles. default run will match production routing (KV enabled). we'll include a flag --disable-cache for the worst-case run.

elaine: last thing: please include a one-line statement we can quote: "Numbers collected on [date] using model X.vY, quantized with QZ-profile-1; see README for methodology."

sam: noted. i'll aim to drop the folder and the tarball by Tue EOD; final blog-ready artifact Wed morning.

elaine: thanks — this will unblock the launch narrative and webinar decks. :rocket:

sam: happy to help. ping me if you want a quick video walkthrough after it's uploaded.
